historical_basis: Slattenpatten or slattenlangpat (literally 'flaccid breasts' or 'saggy long breast') is a female creature of Danish folklore. Slattenpatten or Slattenlangpat is a female being of Danish folk belief, especially tied to Suså; also called ellekvinde, ellekone or elverkone, and unlike the usually very beautiful ellepige she is marked by extraordinarily long breasts. Her breasts hang down to the waist but can be thrown over the shoulder so a child on her back can feed, and when chased she flings them over her shoulders; in southern Zealand legends tell of her being hunted by 'Kong Volmer' (really Valdemar Atterdag) or 'Wojens Jæger' with hounds. Another legend says her breasts were long so she could suckle her fish-children under water; slattenlangpat is therefore also linked with water and considered a water goddess, especially in Zealand according to some archaeologists.
